sasoestpatrokli.name: St. Patrokli Cathedral
sasoestpatrokli.slogan: Soest's Romanesque tower, seen for miles across the Börde.
sasoestpatrokli.line: Its roughly 80 m tower is called the "Turm Westfalens" and often named Germany's most beautiful Romanesque tower.

sasoestwiese.name: Wiesenkirche
sasoestwiese.slogan: Twin Gothic spires and a Last Supper painted in 1500.
sasoestwiese.line: Founded in 1313, its twin west towers were only finished in 1874-75, after a 350-year pause.

samoehnestaumauer.name: Möhne Dam
samoehnestaumauer.slogan: A great wall of stone holding back the Sauerland's biggest lake.
samoehnestaumauer.line: Built 1908-1913, it was breached by the Dambusters on the night of 16-17 May 1943, and the flood killed at least 1,579 people.

sakroenchenkirche.name: Nikolaikirche and its Krönchen
sakroenchenkirche.slogan: An eight-sided church wearing a golden crown over Siegen.
sakroenchenkirche.line: The gilded coronet on its tower has earned Siegen the nickname "Krönchenstadt".

saattahoehle.name: Atta Cave
saattahoehle.slogan: Fifty-two chambers of dripstone beneath Attendorn.
saattahoehle.line: Found by accident in 1907 in a quarry, it formed 400 million years ago and is Germany's most visited show cave.
